title: From Outliers to Topics in Language Models: Anticipating Trends in News Corpora
subcategory: outliers as weak signals in cumulative BERTopic clustering
task: Testing whether HDBSCAN outliers later become topics in news streams
problem: Density-based topic models discard outliers as noise, although they might be early signals of emerging topics.
architecture: Embeddings from nine pretrained language models (headline, body or full article), UMAP to 2-10 dimensions, cumulative BERTopic/HDBSCAN clustering over 20 monthly windows; outliers (label -1) tracked for conversion into clusters; configuration chosen by silhouette; inter-model agreement and lexical/stylistic analysis of converted vs non-converted outliers.
llm_or_encoder: nine sentence-embedding models (e.g. multilingual-e5-large, paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2, xlm-roberta-large, sentence-camembert-base)

datasets.name: TP
datasets.details: 102 French news articles on corporate social responsibility

datasets.name: GHG
datasets.details: 312 English news articles on climate change

metrics: Kruskal-Wallis tests on TF-IDF and stylistic features
key_results: Average validation of the outlier-to-topic hypothesis 0.80 (French) and 0.81 (English); inter-model agreement 0.7002 and 0.6783.
Silhouette scores 0.61 (French) and 0.52 (English) for the chosen configurations.
strengths: Reframes topic-model outliers as potential early signals; robust across nine models and two languages.

limitations.text: Pilot with small corpora (102 and 312 articles); generalisability limited; larger corpora left for future work.
